articles.title: Rust infrastructure Q3 2026: crates.io, docs.rs and resilient builds

images.alt: A refined architectural library has separate jade-lit entrances for package archives and documentation, connected by orderly protected brass routes.
images.caption: Package availability and documentation availability support development, while build correctness still requires independent checks.

images.alt: Four independent checks ask whether a service is reachable, an artifact is expected, source compiles, and runtime behavior is correct.
images.caption: These checks complement one another. Passing an earlier stage does not prove the later stages.

articles.title: Rust memoization: cache keys, limits and failure handling

images.alt: An elegant observatory indexes luminous calculation tokens into individual drawers and returns a previously stored matching token.
images.caption: Reuse an answer only when the key captures every input that can change its meaning.

images.alt: A table maps Fibonacci inputs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 to 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 and shows a repeated fib(5) returning the cached value 5.
images.caption: Six distinct inputs are cached after fib(5). This is a state illustration, not a call-count or speed benchmark.

articles.title: Cargo build.rs: generated code and reliable rebuilds

images.alt: An ivory specification card enters a brass and glass source foundry and emerges as neatly stacked generated sheets.
images.caption: A generator is an explicit transformation from declared inputs to source that the compiler can consume.

images.alt: A greeting file and GREETING_STYLE feed build.rs on the host, which writes OUT_DIR/generated.rs for rustc compiling the target.
images.caption: Both inputs are tracked explicitly. The generator runs on the host; its generated source is compiled for the selected target.
